Tanzid urges Bangladesh batters to take responsibility
item.description:
Bangladesh opener Tanzid Hasan Tamim has urged his teammates to take the onus and improve their awareness ahead of the game against Afghanistan, a match that is crucial for them to reach tri-nation One Day International (ODI) series final.

The Afghanistan game turned out to be a must-win match for Bangladesh following their 99-run defeat to Zimbabwe in the opening match. Not only a victory would give Bangladesh an edge, but also they have to overcome a net-run-rate issue.

Due to vulnerable batting, Bangladesh failed to chase down 272, set by Zimbabwe in a batting-favourable condition. It prompted pacer Taskin Ahmed to express concern over the team's lack of consistency and game awareness earlier a day ago.

Today, ahead of the crucial Afghanistan match, Tanzid agreed with Taskin's assessment, admitting that the batters had failed to take responsibility while chasing the target.

"What he (Taskin) said is true. We could not take responsibility in our batting unit. The wicket was good enough, and I think the target was chase-able," Tanzid said in a video footage sent by the Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB).

"I felt very good as long as I batted. Unfortunately, I got out. But I think we all should take responsibility."

 The opener said Bangladesh's batters need to approach challenging targets with a more positive and practical mindset, breaking them down into smaller goals rather than focusing on the overall total.

"Of course, it is a matter of mindset. If we play with small targets instead of thinking about 300 or 350, then things will be easier. This is how we have to set our mentality," he said.

"I think consistency and mindset are very important here. If these two come together, we will be able to do well in difficult situations."

Tanzid also acknowledged that Bangladesh had been outplayed by Zimbabwe, attributing the defeat primarily to his team's failure to perform to its potential rather than the opposition's superiority alone.

"We didn't play good cricket; they played better than us. That's why they won and we lost," he said.

item.title: Execution of 2 Bangladeshis in Saudi Arabia: What does the consulate’s letter say?
item.description:
Saudi authorities did not inform the Bangladesh Embassy or consulate in advance about the execution of two Bangladeshi nationals. Nor did they formally notify the Bangladeshi authorities after carrying out the executions.

This information was disclosed in a letter sent by the Labour Welfare Wing of the Bangladesh Consulate General in Jeddah to the Ministry of Expatriates’ Welfare and Overseas Employment on 18 October.

The letter stated that the executions came to light through reports in several Saudi media outlets, citing a statement issued by the country’s Ministry of Interior on 14 October.

The two Bangladeshis executed were Nazrul Islam Abdul Bashir and Sweety Akter. According to information in the Saudi Interior Ministry’s statement, as reported by Saudi media, the executions took place in the Mecca region. They were accused of engaging in immoral acts inside a mosque in the holy city of Mecca, thereby violating its sanctity.

The consulate’s letter noted that Saudi authorities had not provided detailed information about the two individuals.

The letter further stated that the Bangladesh Consulate in Jeddah had requested information from the Saudi Ministry of Foreign Affairs about Bangladeshis detained for various offences in prisons across western Saudi Arabia.

In response to that request, a list was received on 30 September. The names of Nazrul and Sweety appeared on the list, but it contained no information about their sentences.

According to the information received, they had been employed as cleaners at a Saudi company named Al Majal.

The list showed that Nazrul had been detained on 1 August 2023 on allegations of information technology-related offences. Sweety was detained the following day on an adultery charge. Nazrul was held at the Jeddah Correctional Facility, while Sweety was detained at the Jeddah Women’s Prison. The letter stated that the list did not mention any sentence imposed on either of them.

The consulate’s letter also noted that there was no known precedent for a Bangladeshi national being sentenced to death in Saudi Arabia for information technology-related offences or adultery.

According to the letter, a list showed that 306 Bangladeshis were being held in prisons across western Saudi Arabia in connection with various morality-related cases. Of them, 147 had been sentenced to prison terms ranging from one month to 15 years.

The consulate stated that neither family had submitted an application seeking legal assistance for the two Bangladeshis, nor had either family contacted the consulate. Saudi authorities had also not informed the Bangladeshi authorities about the death sentences or their execution.

The consulate added that it had sent a diplomatic note to the Mecca branch of the Saudi Ministry of Foreign Affairs seeking copies of the judgments and detailed information about the cases. A comprehensive report would be submitted once the copies of the judgments were received.

item.title: French PM to meet unions as govt prepares for more protests
item.description:
FRANCE-SOCIAL-DEMO-CURFEW

France's prime minister plans to meet unions on Wednesday to discuss security and has vowed a "massive" police deployment at protests, following riots in the past week that led to curfews and arrests.

The eurozone's second-largest economy was rocked on the weekend by some of its worst rioting in recent years, just six months before voters head to the polls to elect a successor to President Emmanuel Macron.

Sebastien Lecornu will meet with representatives from five unions on Wednesday morning to discuss "ways and means to guarantee the essential freedom to demonstrate" according to a letter sent to the organisations, which noted some were attempting to subvert the protests with "unacceptable acts."

More protests centred over rising living costs are planned on Saturday, organised by the "Yellow Vest" movement and high school students, with another called for November 5 by labour unions.

School students have not been invited to the Wednesday meeting.

Images of clashes, mobs looting stores and public buildings set ablaze last weekend prompted several countries, including the United States, China and Germany, to issue travel advisories for their citizens in France.

Facing angry lawmakers in parliament, Lecornu acknowledged that the security response had fallen short and promised a stronger approach ahead of the new wave of protests.

"The deployment for next Saturday will be massive," Lecornu said.

Arrests and investigations

French authorities announced on Monday partial curfews in Paris and other cities, and Lecornu said fresh ones would be imposed on Tuesday where needed.

The nighttime curfew in the capital, from 2100 GMT Tuesday, applied to Republique square in the centre-east and Les Halles shopping district in the centre.

A ban on public gatherings was also ordered for the Champs-Elysees, near several public buildings, and at train stations.

Paris police ordered a temporary ban on people carrying cans or bottles of petrol or gas, after mobs set fire to government buildings and shops last weekend.

Security forces arrested a man believed to be connected to the ultra-left over the burning down of a historic town hall in Limoges, whose destruction has become a symbol of the violence.

Authorities have faced criticism from parties across the political spectrum, with far-right presidential candidate Marine Le Pen describing the unrest as a "wake-up call" that exposed a "profound crisis" of authority.

Recent polling suggests Le Pen leading first-round presidential voting intentions by a wide margin and far-left candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon emerging as the strongest contender for the runoff.

Lecornu has accused ultra-left radical groups of forging an "insurrectionary plan" that led to the riots.

In a sign of growing political scrutiny over the street violence, lawmakers from across France's fractured parliament agreed on Tuesday to launch a parliamentary inquiry into the unrest, including possible intelligence failures, policing tactics and the government's preparedness.

Investors have sold off French debt in recent weeks amid rising doubts about the government's ability to rein in spending.

Nearly 150 people had been jailed and more than 800 brought before the courts, according to the justice minister.

Interior Minister Laurent Nunez offered to resign on Sunday, saying police "had lost control" during the unrest. Macron rejected his resignation and Nunez was also set to attend Wednesday's meeting with union representatives.

Other European countries have seen demonstrations over rising prices, with smaller clashes breaking out in Italy's financial centre of Milan as well as in Belgium over the weekend.

US President Donald Trump has seized on the unrest in France to amplify his anti-immigration and anti-Islam rhetoric, at a time when his Republican party is facing headwinds in upcoming midterm elections.

Trump launched into a lengthy tirade at a midterms rally Monday in Kansas, saying France was being "conquered, looted, and burned to the ground by migrants, jihadists, and communists."

Several analysts have countered Trump's rhetoric, saying immigration was not a driving force in France's unrest.

item.title: PSG sink Barcelona in six-goal thriller, Liverpool and Man City win
item.description:
SOCCER-CHAMPIONS-PSG-BAR/

Paris St Germain underlined their status as European champions by beating Barcelona 4-2 in a blockbuster Champions League clash on Tuesday, while Liverpool and Manchester City also claimed victories.

Desire Doue, Lucas Hernandez, Vitinha and Fabian Ruiz scored for PSG, with Xavi Espart and Lamine Yamal twice pulling Barcelona level in the second half.

Alexis Mac Allister scored twice as Liverpool fought back from two goals down to beat Villarreal 4-3 in a thrilling encounter at Anfield.

Phil Foden scored a hat-trick to lead Manchester City to a 5-1 win over AEK Athens at the Etihad Stadium, with Elliot Anderson and Rayan Cherki also on the scoresheet as Erling Haaland was rested.

PSG outlast Barcelona

Barcelona arrived at the Parc des Princes with a perfect record across all competitions this season, but PSG proved more clinical in a breathless contest to hand the Catalans their first defeat of the campaign.

The relentless tempo took its toll, with PSG's Ousmane Dembele, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Marquinhos, along with Barcelona's Dani Olmo, all forced off through injury.

PSG peppered the Barcelona goal in the opening five minutes, with Kvaratskhelia hitting the post, before the game settled into a rhythm.

The hosts gradually took control of midfield and went ahead after Yamal surrendered possession in his own half, allowing Doue to drive a fierce low shot into the corner.

Goalkeeper Joan Garcia produced several saves to keep Barcelona in the contest before Espart, making his first Champions League start, created and finished a superb move to equalise in the 55th minute.

Ferran Torres hit the post against his former club before Hernandez headed PSG in front from a corner in the 72nd minute, starting a burst of four goals in 14 minutes.

Lamine equalised again for Barcelona with a brilliant individual effort in the 79th minute, before Vitinha responded for PSG with a fine strike 109 seconds later.

As Hansi Flick's side searched for an equaliser, Fabian Ruiz converted an Achraf Hakimi cross at the back post to seal the victory.

The result lifted PSG onto nine points and top of the Champions League standings, ahead of Liverpool on goal difference.

Foden hits three

Foden netted a hat-trick as Man City comfortably dispatched AEK Athens at the Etihad Stadium.

Anderson opened the scoring for the hosts in the 12th minute before Foden doubled the advantage in the 34th.

AEK Athens pulled a goal back through Stavros Pilios in the 52nd minute, but Cherki restored City's two-goal cushion five minutes later.

Foden added his second of the night in the 65th minute and completed his treble 11 minutes later to wrap up a dominant performance.

Haaland was an unused substitute, as City gave their leading striker a rest amid a demanding fixture schedule.

Liverpool edged Spanish side Villarreal after a stirring comeback.

The visitors stunned the home crowd when Georges Mikautadze struck in the fourth minute before Sergi Cardona doubled Villarreal's lead in the 29th.

Liverpool's fightback started with two headers as Mac Allister pulled a goal back in the 36th minute before Ronald Araujo equalised in first-half stoppage time.

Mac Allister completed the turnaround with his second goal in the 65th minute, and Florian Wirtz hammered home a fourth in the 69th to cap a rampant spell for the hosts.

Tani Oluwaseyi pulled one back for Villarreal in the 87th minute, but Liverpool survived the late pressure to secure the points.

Atletico Madrid's Julian Alvarez levelled in the second half to earn them a 1-1 draw with VfB Stuttgart, who took the lead through Jamie Leweling before the break. Morten Hjulmand was sent off in the 64th minute, leaving Atletico with 10 men for the closing stages.

Napoli edged Bodo/Glimt 4-3 and PSV Eindhoven held off Porto for a 1-0 win, while AS Roma cruised to a 4-0 victory over Slovan Bratislava.

Earlier, Borussia Dortmund won 2-1 against Champions League debutants Sabah, while a 90th-minute equaliser from Pavel Kacor earned Slavia Prague a point in a 2-2 draw at Fenerbahce.

item.title: Bangladesh face Afghanistan in a must-win game
item.description:
Bangladesh face an uphill task in their bid to reach the final of the tri-nation One Day International (ODI) series in the United Arab Emirates (UAE), with an in-form Afghanistan standing in their way.

Following a 99-run defeat to Zimbabwe in the opening match, Bangladesh are in a must-win situation as they take on Afghanistan in their final group-stage match at Sheikh Zayed Stadium in Abu Dhabi on Wednesday. The match will begin at 5.30 PM, Bangladesh time.

A victory would keep Bangladesh in contention for a place in the final, but they would also need to negotiate the tricky net run-rate equation.

Net run-rate equation

Afghanistan hold a strong advantage after registering a massive 158-run victory over Zimbabwe. Their commanding net run rate means they could still qualify for the final even if they lose to Bangladesh.

Bangladesh, however, could overtake Zimbabwe in the standings on net run rate if they manage to beat Afghanistan by a substantial margin.

Afghanistan currently top the standings with a net run rate of +3.160 after winning their only match. Zimbabwe are second at -0.590, having won one and lost one, while Bangladesh sit third at -1.980 following their opening defeat.

Recent head-to-head results suggest that overcoming Afghanistan won’t be a cake-walk for Bangladesh.

The two sides have met 22 times in ODIs, with both winning 11 matches. However, Afghanistan have dominated their last six encounters, winning five. All five victories came at UAE venues in Sharjah and Abu Dhabi.

Bangladesh lost a three-match ODI series in Sharjah 2-1 in 2024. Their struggles continued in 2025, when Afghanistan swept a three-match series in Abu Dhabi, including a humiliating 200-run defeat.

In that match, played on 14 October 2025, Bangladesh were bowled out for just 93 after Afghanistan posted 293-9.

One year and six days after that heavy defeat, Bangladesh will face Afghanistan again in the ODI format, hoping to reverse their fortunes.

The two teams also played a one-off Test earlier this month, which ended in a draw despite Afghanistan being in a difficult position. The result could provide Afghanistan with an additional psychological boost ahead of the ODI encounter.

Winning the toss, however, could prove crucial for Bangladesh. The Abu Dhabi surface generally becomes slower as the match progresses, making batting under lights in the second innings increasingly difficult.

The tournament’s last two matches have underlined the challenges teams face when batting second under lights.

Bangladesh head coach Phil Simmons has emphasised the importance of batting out the full 50 overs, saying greater awareness of the match situation could have changed the outcome against Zimbabwe.

“We lacked understanding of the situation, and making sure that when we got the three wickets, we hammer down and try and get another one quickly. Although, they batted really well,” Simmons said.

“But then when we batted, we just lacked the understanding of the situation and knowing that with a start like that, we just had to make sure we bat for the 50 overs and we’d have won the game,” he added.

Bangladesh have already suffered a setback with regular captain Liton Das ruled out of the entire tournament because of a hip injury.

However, allrounder Mehidy Hasan could return to the side after missing the opening match due to fever.

item.title: Deceived into fighting for Russia, Bangladeshi families now battle debt
item.description:
Pabitra Chandra was born into an impoverished family in Gopalpur, Tangail. He worked as a carpenter and earned very little. Hoping for a better future, he sold some of his wife’s gold jewellery and borrowed money from a microfinance organisation and local moneylenders before travelling to Russia.

Although he had been promised a job, he and 29 other Bangladeshi nationals were forcibly sent to the Russia-Ukraine battlefield. His family learned from surviving companions that Pabitra had died in the fighting. Now, alongside their grief, the family faces relentless demands from creditors to repay the money they borrowed.

Pabitra Chandra’s family is not alone. The families of the 30 young Bangladeshi men who were deceived into travelling to Russia for work are facing similar hardships.

Reports indicate that 20 of the 30, including Pabitra, have died. Two others were injured and are receiving treatment at hospitals in Russia, while two have managed to return to Bangladesh. The remaining six are still being forced to fight on the battlefield.

At a press conference on 14 October, the Special Response Battalion (SRB) said that the 30 Bangladeshis had travelled to Russia on 7 May through three organisations named Jabal-e-Noor, RS International and TS Group. Each man was charged an average of Tk 1 million on the promise of employment at construction companies.

After they arrived in Russia, however, their passports and mobile phones were confiscated, and they were handed over to the Russian military instead of being given the promised jobs.

Following 21 days of military training, they were deployed to the Russia-Ukraine battlefield. Seventeen of the 30 were killed in drone strikes on the very first day. Three more died at different times afterwards.

Families in desperate circumstances

Pabitra Chandra, 30, has two daughters aged six and eight. After hearing reports of his death, his wife developed psychological problems. Sometimes she laughs, sometimes she cries.

Pabitra had travelled to Russia with Tk 130,000 raised by selling his wife’s jewellery and another Tk 950,000 borrowed from a microfinance organisation and local moneylenders.

Pabitra’s brother-in-law, Tapan Chandra Sutradhar, told Prothom Alo that the family had been in contact with him for the first few days after he arrived in Russia. At the time, Pabitra said that he and several others were staying at a hotel and would be given jobs once their paperwork was completed.

Bangladeshis sent to Russia for jobs, used as 'prey' in war, 20 killed: SRB

After contact was lost for some time, he called his family on 29 May and said, “They are forcing us to go to war. The risk of dying there is 95 per cent.”

Pabitra subsequently contacted the Bangladesh embassy and requested assistance in arranging the return of himself and the others to Bangladesh. He also apologised to his family for his mistakes.

The family later learned of his death from his companions. However, neither the embassy nor any government source has officially confirmed the news to them.

Tapan Chandra said, “The family has reached such a desperate situation that when they sit down to eat, creditors come and stand behind them demanding money. They are now considering selling the remaining three decimals of land, but even that will not be enough to repay the loans. Still, the family’s last hope is that Pabitra might be alive.”

Robin Mir used to drive an auto-rickshaw in Siddhirganj, Narayanganj. He, too, travelled to Russia in search of work after selling land and livestock in his village and taking out loans. Three other men from Narayanganj went with him. His family learned of his death through them.

Robin’s nephew, Rahat Chowdhury, told Prothom Alo that his uncle was given good food and taken sightseeing for the first three or four days after arriving in Russia. Then the family heard nothing from him for five or six days.

How middlemen recruit Bangladeshi youth for Russia-Ukraine war

On 15 May, Robin informed them that they were being taken to work. Contact was subsequently lost again. On 17 May, the family saw him in a video from a military camp.

On 29 May, Robin called his family in tears and said, “They promised us jobs, but took us through a dense forest and sold us off.”

That was the last time Rahat spoke to his uncle.

Rahat said his uncle’s wife and two children were now living in desperate circumstances. The daughter is nine years old and the son is five. Creditors call repeatedly and subject the family to verbal abuse. Sometimes, the family has enough food for one meal but nothing for the next.

In addition to Pabitra and Robin, Prothom Alo spoke to family members of seven of the 30 Bangladeshis who travelled to Russia. Almost all the families are from low-income backgrounds.

According to information provided by the families, the other 18 men reported killed on the battlefield are Sohel, Md Mehedi Hasan, Md Al Mamun, Md Abdullah Al Mamun, Md Nazmul Alam, Md Wasim Akram, Md Arif Hossain, Md Sayeed Molla, Tarikul Islam Mintu, Sabbir Hossain, Mofiz, Md Arman Ali, Md Nazrul Islam, Md Aminul Islam, Kazi Rezaul Karim, Main Uddin, Ripon Hossain and Arif Hossain Patwary.

Of the 30 Bangladeshis who were deceived, Rajon Hossain and Adnan Hossain have managed to return to Bangladesh. Palash Sheikh and Ali Hasan Sohel were injured and are receiving treatment at hospitals in Russia.

6 still on the battlefield

Roni Sheikh of Gopalganj, Al Amin Islam of Lalmonirhat, Sourav Molla of Gopalganj, Kamal Hossain of Madaripur, Abu Hanif of Kishoreganj and Helal Sheikh of Madaripur are still being forced to fight on the Russia-Ukraine battlefield. Some of them remain in contact with their families.

Taslim Sardar, the husband of Sourav Molla’s younger sister, regularly communicates with Sourav through the messaging app Imo.

Taslim told Prothom Alo that Sourav was currently stationed three to four kilometres behind the frontline. He was being made to dig earth for bunkers, and something could happen to him at any time. He had tried to escape twice but had failed.

Taslim recently joined the families of the victims in holding a human chain protest in Dhaka.

He said Kamal was working alongside Sourav, digging earth for bunkers. Roni Sheikh and Al Amin were walking from their camp to the frontline to deliver food, water and weapons. Hanif and Helal had no fixed duties. They were assigned various tasks, including digging bunker trenches and delivering food.

item.title: Bijoya Dashami Wednesday as Durga Puja concludes with idol immersion
item.description:
Sharadiya Durga Puja, the largest religious festival of the Hindu community, concludes on Wednesday with the immersion of idols on the occasion of Bijoya Dashami.
After five days of rituals and festivities, Goddess Durga is set to return to her heavenly abode at Kailash, leaving devotees with a sense of melancholy at puja mandaps across the country.
Devotees have been gathering at puja mandaps since morning to mark Bijoya Dashami. As they bid farewell to the Goddess, they are offering prayers for peace, prosperity and well-being for their families, society and the nation.
According to schedules released by the Mahanagar Sarbajanin Puja Committee and Dhakeshwari National Temple authorities, the Dashami Bihita Puja and Darpan Bisarjan, the symbolic immersion of the deity’s reflection, are scheduled to be completed by 9:57am.
The day's key rituals include Devi Baran and Sindur Khela. Before the immersion, married women bid farewell to the Goddess by applying vermilion to her and offering sweets, praying for their husbands' longevity and the happiness, well-being and prosperity of their families.
They then apply vermilion, first touched to the Goddess's feet, to one another's foreheads and cheeks. The ritual is accompanied by dance, music and the exchange of sweets. Unmarried women and other devotees also join the festivities.
According to the schedule, Devi Baran is set to begin at 11:30am, followed by a voluntary blood donation program at noon.

item.title: Intern doctors at RMCH halt work over five-point demand
item.description:
Intern doctors at Rajshahi Medical College Hospital launched a 24-hour work stoppage at 8am on Wednesday, pressing for a five-point set of demands, including addressing shortages of medical supplies and improving security.
The work stoppage has disrupted medical services at the hospital, causing hardship for patients, many of whom have travelled from distant areas, and their relatives.
The protesting doctors said essential medicines and medical supplies were in short supply in the hospital’s inpatient wards. They also complained of difficulties caused by the unrestricted entry of patients’ relatives into the wards and alleged negligence by Ansar personnel responsible for security. They further claimed to have faced organized threats.
The interns said the hospital’s observation room and casualty department were currently non-functional, increasing the pressure on inpatient wards. They said limited staffing and inadequate medical supplies had made it difficult to provide proper care.
According to the protesters, the hospital administration had repeatedly assured them that the problems would be addressed but had taken no effective steps. They said the work stoppage was a last resort.
Dr S M Tapu, president of the Intern Doctors’ Society at Rajshahi Medical College Hospital, said a press conference would be held on Wednesday afternoon to outline the demands, explain the situation and announce their next course of action.

item.title: Dhaka ranks 9th among world’s most polluted cities
item.description:
Dhaka ranked 9th among the world's most polluted cities on Wednesday morning, recording an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 162 at 10:05am.
The air quality was classified as "unhealthy", meaning the concentration of pollutants in the air had reached a level that could pose health risks to the general population, according to the AQI scale.
Lahore in Pakistan ranked first with an AQI score of 272, while Delhi in India ranked second with a score of 249, followed by Jakarta in Indonesia third place with an AQI score of 183.
According to AQI standards, a reading between 101 and 150 is considered "unhealthy for sensitive groups", while 151 to 200 is classified as "unhealthy". A reading between 201 and 300 is considered "very unhealthy", while levels above 301 are deemed "hazardous", posing serious health risks.
The AQI provides daily updates on air quality, indicating how clean or polluted the air is and highlighting potential health impacts.
In Bangladesh, the AQI is calculated based on five major pollutants: particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO), sulfur dioxide (SO2) and ozone.
Dhaka has long struggled with air pollution, with air quality typically deteriorating during winter and improving during the monsoon season.
The World Health Organization estimates that air pollution causes around seven million deaths globally each year, mainly from stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer and acute respiratory infections.

item.title: Bangladesh face Afghanistan for must-win tri-nation ODI
item.description:
Bangladesh face an uphill task in their bid to reach the final of the tri-nation ODI series in the United Arab Emirates (UAE), with an in-form Afghanistan standing in their way.
Following a 99-run defeat to Zimbabwe in the opening match, Bangladesh are in a must-win situation as they take on Afghanistan in their final group-stage match at Sheikh Zayed Stadium in Abu Dhabi on Wednesday.
The match will begin at 5.30 PM, Bangladesh time.
A victory would keep Bangladesh in contention for a place in the final, but they would also need to negotiate the tricky net run-rate equation.
Afghanistan hold a strong advantage after registering a massive 158-run victory over Zimbabwe. Their commanding net run rate means they could still qualify for the final even if they lose to Bangladesh.
Bangladesh, however, could overtake Zimbabwe in the standings on net run rate if they manage to beat Afghanistan by a substantial margin.
Afghanistan currently top the standings with a net run rate of +3.160 after winning their only match. Zimbabwe are second at -0.590, having won one and lost one, while Bangladesh sit third at -1.980 following their opening defeat.
Recent head-to-head results suggest that overcoming Afghanistan won't be a cake-walk for Bangladesh. The two sides have met 22 times in ODIs, with both winning 11 matches. However, Afghanistan have dominated their last six encounters, winning five. All five victories came at UAE venues in Sharjah and Abu Dhabi.
Bangladesh lost a three-match ODI series in Sharjah 2-1 in 2024. Their struggles continued in 2025, when Afghanistan swept a three-match series in Abu Dhabi, including a humiliating 200-run defeat.
In that match, played on October 14, 2025, Bangladesh were bowled out for just 93 after Afghanistan posted 293-9.
One year and six days after that heavy defeat, Bangladesh will face Afghanistan again in the ODI format, hoping to reverse their fortunes.
The two teams also played a one-off Test earlier this month, which ended in a draw despite Afghanistan being in a difficult position. The result could provide Afghanistan with an additional psychological boost ahead of the ODI encounter.
Winning the toss, however, could prove crucial for Bangladesh. The Abu Dhabi surface generally becomes slower as the match progresses, making batting under lights in the second innings increasingly difficult.
The tournament's last two matches have underlined the challenges teams face when batting second under lights.
Bangladesh head coach Phil Simmons has emphasised the importance of batting out the full 50 overs, saying greater awareness of the match situation could have changed the outcome against Zimbabwe.
"We lacked understanding of the situation, and making sure that when we got the three wickets, we hammer down and try and get another one quickly. Although, they batted really well," Simmons said.
"But then when we batted, we just lacked the understanding of the situation and knowing that with a start like that, we just had to make sure we bat for the 50 overs and we'd have won the game," he added.
Bangladesh have already suffered a setback with regular captain Liton Das ruled out of the entire tournament because of a hip injury.
However, allrounder Mehidy Hasan could return to the side after missing the opening match due to fever.

item.title: PSG late show downs Barca in Champions League, Liverpool fight back in 7-goal thriller
item.description:
Holders Paris Saint-Germain made it three wins from three in this season's Champions League, beating Barcelona 4-2 thanks to late goals from Vitinha and Fabian Ruiz on Tuesday, while Liverpool clinched a dramatic comeback victory over Villarreal.
Phil Foden scored a hat-trick as Manchester City thrashed AEK Athens 5-1, while there were also much-needed wins for Roma and Napoli.
PSG kept their place at the top of the league-phase table, but could yet count the cost of injuries suffered by Ousmane Dembele, Marquinhos and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia at the Parc des Princes.
"We don't feel superior to any team but we trust in ourselves, in everyone who starts and who comes off the bench," Paris midfielder Ruiz told Movistar. "There's still a long way to go."
Barcelona twice levelled against the two-time defending champions, but were ultimately well beaten as they slipped to their first defeat of the season.
"We tried to play how we want to play, we pressed them very high. There were a lot of fantastic things on show today," said Flick, whose team had won their previous 11 games in all competitions this term.
Kvaratskhelia hit the post, Dembele hobbled off and Ferran Torres was denied by Barca goalkeeper Joan Garcia in a fast-paced opening.
PSG took a deserved lead in the 38th minute as Desire Doue collected the ball outside the area and thumped a shot into the bottom corner.
Garcia made another excellent save shortly after the break from Achraf Hakimi, before Xavi Espart burst through to level for Barca against the run of play.
Kvaratskhelia and Marquinhos both pulled up injured within seconds of each other and had to leave the field.
The home team continued to press, though, and Lucas Hernandez restored their advantage 18 minutes from time with a brilliant header.
Lamine Yamal powered past Warren Zaire-Emery to equalise again seven minutes later.
But Vitinha hammered home from outside the box in the 81st minute and Ruiz's tap-in gave Luis Enrique's team a second straight 4-2 Champions League win after seeing off Man City by the same scoreline last week.
Liverpool battled back from two goals down to also maintain their 100-percent record by edging out Villarreal 4-3 at Anfield.
Liverpool fell behind in the fourth minute when Georges Mikautadze pounced on a terrible error from Virgil van Dijk, before Villarreal defender Sergi Cardona strolled through their defence to make it two.
Alexis Mac Allister pulled one back for the hosts nine minutes before half-time by heading in Kostas Tsimikas's corner.
Andoni Iraola's men were level in first-half added time through Ronald Araujo's back-post header after Cardona inexplicably left Rio Ngumoha's cross.
Mac Allister completed the turnaround by firing in from Ngumoha's square pass, and half-time substitute Florian Wirtz's first goal of the season gave the Reds some breathing space.
Tani Oluwaseyi set up a nervy finish for Iraola, but Liverpool held on.
"We are facing very good teams. It's good to come back but we've started losing too many goals this season," Iraola told Amazon Prime.
At the Etihad, Elliot Anderson put Manchester City in front with his first goal for the club, before Phil Foden made it two goals in as many games after scoring against Ipswich at the weekend.
AEK halved the deficit early in the second half through Stavros Pilios, only for Rayan Cherki to sweep in City's third in the 57th minute.
Foden later fired in his second and third goals in a comprehensive victory, despite Erling Haaland being rested after picking up a knock at the weekend.
"Slowly, but surely. Still got a long way to go, but I am going in the right direction," Foden told TNT Sports of his gradual return to form.
Roma eased to their first Champions League win since 2019 as the capital club brushed aside pointless Slovan Bratislava 4-0 at the Stadio Olimpico.
All four Serie A clubs in the competition lost last week, but Napoli made it two wins from two on Tuesday for the Italian sides.
Massimiliano Allegri's men were twice pegged back by Bodo/Glimt but eventually got the better of the Norwegians in a 4-3 thriller, as Scott McTominay scored a brace.
Atletico Madrid played out a 1-1 draw with Stuttgart in Germany, despite playing much of the second half with 10 men.
Borussia Dortmund ended a run of four straight away defeats in the Champions League with a 2-1 win over Sabah in Baku.

item.title: Trump says he wants Zelensky to 'make a deal' with Russia
item.description:
US President Donald Trump on Tuesday urged Volodymyr Zelensky to make a deal with Russia -- redoubling pressure on the Ukrainian leader even as Moscow grinds on with the war it launched four years ago.
Trump also said he had asked Russian President Vladimir Putin to release Stephen Hubbard -- an American taken captive by Moscow's forces years earlier in Ukraine -- in a fresh sign of his pivot back to Moscow.
"We want Zelensky to make a deal. He can make a deal. He could have made a deal two years ago when we had our little chat in the Oval Office," Trump told reporters in the same room.
Trump, Vice President JD Vance and Zelensky had a bruising televised confrontation in the Oval Office in February 2025, shortly after the Ukraine-skeptic US president returned to office.
"He's going to have to want to make a deal, because I don't think his people are going to stand for it any longer," Trump said Tuesday.
Relations between Kyiv and Washington have soured since Trump partially lifted sanctions to strike a diesel-supply deal with Putin and slammed Zelensky as a warmonger for Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil refineries.
The Ukrainian leader met Trump's envoy Steve Witkoff in Oslo on Tuesday for talks aimed at easing the tensions.
Zelensky hailed the resumption of US intelligence sharing on looming Russian strikes, but insisted Kyiv must be included in any future talks on its fate after meetings with US envoys.
Ukraine has been increasingly alarmed by Trump's return to effectively blaming Kyiv for a failure to end the war that began with Moscow's February 2022 invasion, and by his warm words towards Putin.
Trump indicated that a deal with Russia to free Hubbard could be near.
"I've been talking to President Putin about Mr Hubbard. I've been talking to him at length. I've asked him to release him. Let's see what happens," Trump said in response to a question from an AFP journalist.
"Just stick with me," Trump added. "Just you remember that question a couple of days from now, because I do things that nobody else can do."

item.title: The ‘disease’ Shakib–Tamim cured is returning to Bangladesh’s batting
item.description:
If life were a cricket match, it would probably resemble Test cricket more than any other format. A long journey spanning five days. Sometimes there is sunshine, sometimes clouds. Sometimes the batters dominate; at other times, the bowlers are in control. Good times come, and bad times follow. Sometimes, it feels as though everything is over. Then, just when all seems lost, a new story begins.

In a way, one-day international cricket is life, too. Only a little shorter. A miniature life spanning 50 overs. There is room to make mistakes, and there is a chance to correct them. With patience, a team can recover from a collapse. But there is one condition: it must survive.

Bangladesh’s ODI journey has been an exciting struggle to survive. There was a time when batting through 50 overs was an achievement in itself. The fragility of Bangladesh’s batting often seemed more frightening than the opposition’s bowling.

Then times changed. Shakib Al Hasan, Tamim Iqbal and Mushfiqur Rahim came along. Bangladesh cricket moved beyond its childhood and into adolescence. Batting through 50 overs was no longer a surprise.

But does time always move forward? Recent statistics on Bangladesh’s ODI batting raise that very question. A problem that had largely been overcome seems to be returning: the old habit of seeing innings crumble before the allotted overs are completed.

Of course, there is no rule that a team must bat for all 50 overs to succeed in an ODI. A side can be bowled out after 40 overs and still win. If its bowlers produce a brilliant performance, even a modest total may be enough. And when chasing, winning a match in 30 overs is certainly a success.

But the equation is different for a team batting first. It has the opportunity to use all 50 overs. If it repeatedly fails to make the most of that opportunity, questions inevitably arise about the depth of its batting, its patience and its ability to build an innings.

Bangladesh’s story, therefore, can be told through one statistic: how often it has been bowled out before completing 50 overs when batting first.

The fragile batting of Bangladesh’s early years

Think back to the early days of Bangladesh cricket. Scoring 200 runs in an ODI was a relief. Reaching 250 was practically a cause for celebration. As soon as the opposition bowlers applied a little pressure, the batting line-up would collapse. It was not unusual to see one batter depart, followed by two more in quick succession.

The numbers tell the same story. Between 2000 and 2010, Bangladesh batted first in 82 ODIs. It failed to complete 50 overs in 48 of them. In other words, its innings ended before the allotted overs were completed in 58.5 per cent of those matches.

Put simply, Bangladesh’s batting could not survive the full 50 overs in nearly six out of every 10 matches.

And what about wins?

Bangladesh won only two of those 48 matches—one against Zimbabwe and the other against Kenya. By contrast, it won 18 matches in which it batted through the full 50 overs. The connection between surviving until the end of an innings and winning was already quite evident.

Of course, batting for 50 overs does not guarantee victory. The total scored, the opposition and the nature of the pitch all matter. Even so, the statistics from that period made one thing clear: if Bangladesh wanted to win, it first had to learn how to survive.

Then the times changed

In cricket, as in life, a change of generation can sometimes mark the beginning of a new era. Shakib, Tamim and Mushfiqur became the faces of that transformation in Bangladesh’s batting. The team gained experience alongside them. It learned how to build an innings, when to attack and when to protect its wickets.

It is difficult to compare the Bangladesh team of 2000–2010 with the side that emerged in the following decade.

Between 2010 and 2020, Bangladesh batted first in 83 ODIs. It failed to complete 50 overs in 28 of them, a rate of 33.7 per cent.

The rate had fallen from 58.5 per cent in the previous decade to 33.7 per cent—a drop of 24.8 percentage points. That was a substantial improvement. A team that once failed to bat out 50 overs in nearly six out of every 10 matches had reduced that figure to about three in every 10.

What better statistical evidence could there be of greater stability in the batting?

Bangladesh also won nine matches during that decade despite failing to complete 50 overs. In matches in which it batted through the full 50 overs, it won 27. In other words, Bangladesh had not only learned to spend more time at the crease; it had also begun turning that resilience into victories.

What do the golden years tell us?

When recalling the most memorable periods in Bangladesh’s ODI history, the years following 2015 stand out.

Shakib was then a world-class all-rounder. Tamim was a dependable presence at the top of the order. Mushfiqur was a major pillar of the middle order. Experience and confidence went hand in hand.

Watching Bangladesh during that period inspired at least one belief: losing two early wickets did not mean everything was over. An innings could still be rebuilt.

But do the statistics from those years tell a different story from the decade as a whole?

Between 2015 and 2020, Bangladesh batted first in 40 ODIs. It failed to complete 50 overs in 13 of them, a rate of 32.5 per cent. The figure for the entire decade was 33.7 per cent. The difference was marginal.

In other words, the improvement in Bangladesh’s batting was not confined to a few years after 2015. It remained broadly consistent throughout the 2010–2020 decade.

This was not a case of Bangladesh producing a few years of good batting and temporarily concealing its old weakness. Rather, the team demonstrated a sustained ability to bat through 50 overs over the course of the decade.

So where has that consistency gone?

New symptoms of an old disease

Bangladesh cricket is no longer where it was in its infancy. Expectations of the team in ODIs have changed, too. The aim is no longer merely to put up a fight; winning matches is now the natural expectation. More is demanded of the generation represented by Najmul Hossain and Litton Das.

Yet the statistics suggest that the team may be moving in the opposite direction.

Since 2020, Bangladesh has batted first in 51 ODIs. It failed to complete 50 overs in 18 of them, a rate of 35.3 per cent.

That is not much higher than the previous decade’s 33.7 per cent—just a difference of 1.6 percentage points. On its own, this may not be cause for serious concern. Such fluctuations are normal in cricket. But the picture becomes less reassuring when the calculation starts in 2023.

Since then, Bangladesh has batted first in 34 ODIs. It failed to complete 50 overs in 14 of them, a rate of 41.2 per cent. That means its innings ended prematurely in more than four out of every 10 matches.

Think about that.

A team that spent more than a decade demonstrating its growing ability to bat through 50 overs now appears to be drifting back towards its old weakness.

Of the 14 matches since 2023 in which Bangladesh failed to complete 50 overs, it won four. In matches where it batted through the full 50 overs, it won eight. Once again, the importance of batting through the innings is apparent.

Are two decades of progress slipping away?

Placing the four sets of statistics side by side makes the evolution of Bangladesh’s ODI batting clearer.

They offer four distinct snapshots of the team’s history. The first reflects inexperience. The second tells a story of growing maturity. The third suggests that progress may have stalled. And the fourth points to the return of an old concern.

A note of caution is necessary, however. A rising rate of innings ending before 50 overs does not automatically mean that batting quality has declined by the same proportion. Sometimes wickets fall as a team tries to score quickly. At other times, the match situation forces batters to take risks.

The strength of the opposition and the nature of the pitch can also affect the figures.

Nor would it be right to deliver a definitive verdict on a long-term decline based on statistics covering only a few years. But the questions are legitimate—and they should be asked.

Are Bangladesh’s batters once again losing the patience required to build an innings? Even when they get off to a good start, are they struggling to turn it into a substantial total? Or has a weakness emerged somewhere in the batting order that repeatedly becomes exposed under pressure?

These statistics alone cannot provide definitive answers. But there is little doubt that the questions need to be investigated.

In 50-over cricket, a good start is not enough. A team must negotiate the middle overs and preserve its resources for the finish. Sometimes it must unleash a storm; at other times, it must weather one. Much like life itself.

Bangladesh cricket once learned these lessons rather well. That is why signs of regression are all the more troubling.

The question is no longer whether Bangladesh can bat for 50 overs. It is whether, after all these years, the team is beginning to forget what it learned.

Perhaps that is the greatest tragedy of a 50-over innings, much like life: finding your way, only to lose it again.

item.title: Rubio questions UN, refuses opinion on protests in India, says "this is a democracy"
item.description:
USA-RUBIO/INDIA

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Wednesday described the term “UN experts” as an “oxymoron” when asked about the United Nations' criticism of India's handling of protests, while declining to weigh in on the issue and saying that domestic political matters must be decided by the people of the country concerned.

Responding to a reporter's question about protests by opposition parties and students in India and the UN experts' allegations of a crackdown, Rubio said he would not get involved in India's internal political affairs.

“Well, the UN experts, yeah. My favourite. The UN experts, or is that an oxymoron?” Rubio remarked.

Clarifying Washington's position, he said, “No, it's a domestic political matter. I mean, I am not going to get involved in their politics. This is a democracy. They have elections here. So I am not going to align on their domestic political matters.”

Rubio said demonstrations and the expression of differing political opinions were part of democratic discourse, distinguishing peaceful protests from riots involving vandalism, arson and destruction of property.

He said the ability of people to express themselves and engage in political debate was an important feature of democratic societies. Citing Cuba as a contrast, Rubio pointed to restrictions faced by opposition voices there, including the risk of imprisonment, oppression or exile.

“But we're not going to comment on internal political matters. That's for the Indian people to decide and navigate,” he said.

Earlier, India exposed the double standards of the United Nations and its frontal organisations have been exposed after contrasting stands taken by the representatives to paint protests in India as an issue of alleged human rights abuse. At the United Nations India stressed that human rights should not be used as an instrument of political pressure or selective targeting of countries.

Indian diplomat Barkha Tamrakar who addressed the Assembly on Tuesday (local time) said that India's constitutional safeguards, including Article 21 of the Constitution, protect human rights and ensure due process, as United Nations experts raised concerns over alleged excessive use of force against protesters and restrictions on peaceful demonstrations.Barkha Tamrakar stressed that human rights should not be used as an instrument of political pressure or selective targeting of countries.

"India firmly opposes any attempt to convert unverified allegations, incomplete statistics, or a report that contains no India country observation into a negative characterization of the world's largest democracy...Human rights should not be used as an instrument of political pressure or selective country targeting,” Tamrakar said, emphasising the need for impartial and evidence-based engagement on human rights issues.

The strong rebuttal came after UN experts had claimed that authorities in India were restricting peaceful assembly and indulging in 'enforced disappearances'. Contrastingly a much milder stand was expressed by UN Human Rights Chief Volker Türk when it came to speaking of the police crackdown on violent protests in France and other parts of Europe. Turk even went to the extent of calling protestors 'vandals'.

India has strongly opposed characterisations based on unverified allegations, incomplete statistics or reports lacking India-specific observations.

item.title: Bijoya Dashami being celebrated with traditional Sindur Khela at mandaps
item.description:
Bijoya Dashami, the final day of the six-day Sharadiya Durga Puja, is being celebrated across the country today, Wednesday, with due religious fervour, traditional rituals and communal harmony.

The celebrations are drawing to a close with the observance of Sindur Khela during the day, followed by the immersion (Bisarjan) of Durga idols in nearby rivers, ponds and other water bodies this evening.

Devotees are also exchanging Bijoya greetings, marking the departure of Goddess Durga from her earthly abode.

Temples across the country, including Dhakeshwari National Temple, Ramna Kali Mandir, Siddheshwari Kalimandir and Ramakrishna Mission and Math, are witnessing large gatherings of worshippers.

Married Hindu women, dressed in traditional white sarees with red borders, are participating in Sindur Khela, one of the most prominent rituals of Bijoya Dashami.

Sindur Khela, meaning the playing with vermilion, is a traditional Hindu ritual observed mainly in Bangladesh and eastern India.

During the ritual, married women offer vermilion and sweets to Goddess Durga following the completion of the final Dashami puja. They then smear vermilion on each other’s foreheads and faces, exchange sweets and pray for marital happiness and prosperity.

Although traditionally observed by women, the ritual has increasingly seen the participation of male devotees in recent years, adding to the festive atmosphere.

Dashami puja was performed at temples and temporary mandaps in the morning, followed by Darpan Bisarjan, a symbolic ritual in which the reflection of the Goddess is immersed before the formal immersion of the idol.

Following the rituals, colourful processions are making their way through city streets towards nearby water bodies for the immersion of the idols.

The idols, traditionally carried on bamboo structures, are now being transported on decorated trucks and pickups, with some taken by boat to the middle of rivers for immersion.

Devotees are chanting traditional slogans such as “Aschhe bochhor abar hobe” (It will happen again next year), expressing their hope for the Goddess’s return next year.

In Dhaka, major mandaps at Dhakeshwari National Temple, Ramakrishna Mission and Math, Kalabagan, Banani, Shakhari Bazar and Ramna Kali Mandir have drawn thousands of devotees since morning.

The immersion ceremonies in the capital are expected to draw large crowds, while law enforcement agencies are maintaining security and taking measures to ensure smooth traffic movement.

Similar celebrations are taking place in major divisional cities, including Chattogram, Rajshahi, Khulna, Sylhet and Barishal, as well as district towns such as Narayanganj, Faridpur, Dinajpur, Jashore, Kushtia, Netrakona, Tangail and Satkhira.

Following the immersion, younger family members seek blessings from elders by touching their feet, while relatives and friends exchange warm embraces and Bijoya greetings.

Traditional sweets, including chomchom, kalojam, sandesh and narkeler naru (coconut and jaggery balls), are being distributed among family members, friends and neighbours as part of the Bijoya celebrations.

item.title: Russia to send first diesel cargo of 40,000 tonnes to US on Thursday
item.description:
RUSSIA-ENERGY

Russia will dispatch its first tanker with diesel for the United States on Thursday, Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said, according to the Vedomosti news outlet, after a deal with US President Donald Trump.

Russia lifted its self-imposed ban on diesel exports on 9 October, introduced to tackle domestic shortages triggered by Ukrainian drone attacks on refineries, after reaching the deal with Trump to supply diesel to global markets.

Novak said on Wednesday the vessel will carry 40,000 metric tons of the fuel, adding that the paperwork on the fuel supply is nearing its completion, according to media reports. He did not name the port from which the cargo will be delivered.

"Additional shipments will follow, of course. There were agreements reached between the two leaders. We will meet the United States' needs, to the extent of our capabilities," RIA news agency quoted Novak as saying.

Trump has said Russia would immediately export 300,000 metric tons, or 2.25 million barrels, followed by 500,000 tons in November and 1 million tons "immediately thereafter".

The US exports about 1.5 million barrels of diesel per day.

Russian President Vladimir Putin was hosting US special envoy Steve Witkoff on Wednesday, after the US-Russia diesel export deal led to a sharp deterioration in ties between the United States and Ukraine.

During the talks in St Petersburg, Witkoff thanked Putin for lifting the export restrictions. Putin also mentioned the deal, saying that diesel prices dropped after the agreement.

item.title: 3 tourists die while bathing at Himchhari beach in Cox’s Bazar, 2 missing
item.description:
Three tourists have died while swimming at Himchhari beach in Cox's Bazar and two others are missing today, Wednesday, around 4: 30 PM at the beach adjacent to the museum of Marina Resort on the Cox's Bazar-Teknaf Marine Drive in Himchhari.

Fire service, lifeguards, and beach workers conducted a search until 7: 30 PM but couldn't find the two missing individuals.

According to police and lifeguard sources, a group of 12 people from Dhaka went to visit Himchhari beach.

Among them, five people went swimming in the sea. At that time, due to a large wave, all five got submerged. Later, lifeguards and locals rescued three of them. However, by then, they had already passed away. Searches are ongoing to find the other two missing individuals.

The three deceased tourists are Md Borhan (23), Saiful Islam (23), and Nafisul Haque (22) from Diabari, Uttara, Dhaka. Their bodies have been taken from Himchhari to the morgue at Cox's Bazar Sadar Hospital at night.

The the incident has been confirmed by the Officer-in-Charge (OC) of Ramu Police Station, AK Fazlul Haque. He told Prothom Alo that operations are ongoing to rescue the two missing individuals.

Imtiaz Ahmed, regional director of the private lifeguard company Sea-Safe, told Prothom Alo that the group of 12 tourists from Dhaka went to the beach adjacent to the museum of Marina Resort in Himchhari, about 9 kilometers south of the city, around 4 PM. Among them, five went swimming in the sea. When they got submerged due to waves, lifeguards and locals quickly initiated rescue efforts. Three were rescued but had already died.

Imtiaz Ahmed stated that from Kolatoli to Laboni Point along the Cox's Bazar sea beach, about five kilometers, Sea-Safe has 27 lifeguards available for rescue operations if someone goes missing while swimming.

However, there aren't enough personnel to conduct rescue operations along the vast stretch of beach from Kolatoli to the south, including Dariyanagar, Himchhari, Patuartek, Inani, and Teknaf.

Imtiaz Ahmed added that over 300,000 tourists are currently in Cox's Bazar. This afternoon, a large crowd gathered at Laboni Point for the immersion festival of idols. Seeing the crowd at various points on the beach, many people are rushing to swim at Dariyanagar and Himchhari beaches, which is increasing the risk of accidents.

According to Imtiaz Ahmed, at least 20 hidden channels have formed at Kolatoli, Sugandha, and Laboni Points, including Himchhari-Dariyanagar. Despite multiple places displaying red flags warning against swimming in dangerous areas, many are not adhering to the warnings.

Currently, more than 300, 000 tourists are staying in Cox''s Bazar. It has been reported by the concerned individuals that no rooms are available in any of the over 500 hotels, guesthouses, resorts, and cottages.
Most recently, on September 27 at Laboni Point on Cox''s Bazar beach, a tourist died from being swept away by the sea.

item.title: Rashid leads Afghanistan rout as Bangladesh crumble for 160
item.description:
Parvez Hossain scored a fighting 70, but Bangladesh were bowled out for 160 in 40 overs against Afghanistan in their must-win match of the tri-nation One Day International series at Sheikh Zayed Stadium in Abu Dhabi on Wednesday.

Leg-spinner Rashid Khan led Afghanistan’s bowling attack with four wickets for 31 runs, including two wickets in consecutive deliveries to wrap up Bangladesh’s innings.

Bangladesh, who elected to bat first, needed to beat Afghanistan by at least 41 runs to qualify for the final. Their hopes now depend on restricting Afghanistan to a sufficiently low total.

Bangladesh suffered an early collapse, losing four wickets for just 28 runs. Tanzid Hasan fell to Yamin Ahmadzai before Soumya Sarkar was bowled off the next ball, leaving the side in deep trouble.

Najmul Hossain offered some resistance with 15 off 23 balls but was caught behind, while captain Towhid Hridoy fell to Azmatullah Omarzai, who took a return catch.

With Bangladesh struggling at 28 for four in the seventh over, Parvez and Saif Hassan came together to rebuild the innings. The pair added 92 runs for the fifth wicket, helping Bangladesh cross 100 after 26 overs.

Parvez reached his half-century off 74 balls, scoring his second ODI fifty after being included in the squad for the tri-series as a replacement for Litton Das.

Saif, however, fell immediately after Parvez reached the milestone, attempting a big shot against Mohammad Nabi and offering a catch to Nangeyalia Kharote at midwicket. He scored 41 off 82 balls.

Mehidy Hasan Miraz lasted just seven deliveries before being caught at backward square leg off Bilal Sami for two.

Parvez continued to fight, bringing up Bangladesh’s 150 with a six off Nabi in the 39th over. But Rashid struck again, bowling Shoriful Islam for seven before trapping Parvez leg-before-wicket for 70 off 96 balls, an innings featuring five fours and two sixes.

Rashid then dismissed debutant Aliss Al Islam, caught by Nabi at slip, before Mustafizur Rahman was bowled first ball. Bangladesh lost their final three wickets in quick succession to finish on 160.
